# laravel_cloud_database (Resource)

Manages a database (schema) within a Laravel Cloud database cluster.

~> **Beta:** This provider is in beta and may change between releases.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_database_cluster" "example" {
  name    = "my-app-db"
  type    = "laravel_mysql"
  version = "8.4"
  region  = "us-east-2"

  # The settings of the database type, as JSON. size is one of the sizes the
  # laravel_cloud_database_types data source lists for the type.
  config = jsonencode({
    size                     = "mysql-flex-1gb"
    storage                  = 10 # GiB
    is_public                = false
    uses_scheduled_snapshots = true
    retention_days           = 7
  })
}

resource "laravel_cloud_database" "example" {
  cluster_id = laravel_cloud_database_cluster.example.id
  name       = "my_app"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Database cluster ID.
- `name` (String) Database name.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `status` (String) Database status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Databases are addressed through their cluster, so the import ID is composite.
terraform import laravel_cloud_database.example "{cluster_id}:{database_id}"
```
